advances: Refutes a universal rank-linear bound on the capacity-weighted entropy-row likelihood variance. A complete almost-Boolean support with uniform original law has an exponentially growing capacity surplus, a uniform directional fourth-moment certificate, and quadratic weighted likelihood variance. Its unique expensive row asymptotically receives all capacity weight, while its contribution to the actual original-law moments tends to zero. Integer-interval padding preserves the obstruction even when the support cardinality divided by the parity-class count tends to infinity. The actual second and third moments nevertheless retain absolute dimensional-scale lower bounds. This disproves the proposed weighted-price bridge and a repair based solely on excluding supports of bounded atom-to-parity ratio; it does not disprove the locked weak Oertel conjecture or a universal actual-moment bound.

proof:
First verify the support geometry. Every point of \(\mathcal P_n\) has a representation \(\mathbf x=(1-t)\mathbf b-t\mathbf1_n\), where \(0\le t\le1\) and \(\mathbf b\in[0,1]^n\). Each coordinate lies in \([-1,1]\). If an integer point has a negative coordinate, that coordinate equals \(-1\), and \((1-t)(b_i+1)=0\) forces \(t=1\). The point is then the apex \(-\mathbf1_n\). If it has no negative coordinates, all its coordinates are zero or one, so it belongs to the cube. Conversely, all the stated points belong to the polytope. This proves completeness. The cube gives full dimension, and the differences \(\mathbf e_i-\mathbf0\) generate the entire lattice \(\mathbb Z^n\).

For a nonzero Boolean point \(\mathbf b\), choose the linear functional whose coefficient in coordinate \(i\) is \(n\) if \(b_i=1\) and \(-1\) if \(b_i=0\). It has a unique maximum on the cube at \(\mathbf b\). If \(|\mathbf b|=k\ge1\), its value there is \(nk>0\), whereas its value at the apex is \(n-(n+1)k\le-1\). Thus it uniquely exposes \(\mathbf b\) on the entire support. The functional \(-\sum_i x_i\) uniquely exposes the apex. To check that the origin is interior, suppose a supporting functional through the origin satisfies \(\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf x\le0\) throughout the polytope. Its values at \(\mathbf e_i\) give \(u_i\le0\), and its value at the apex gives \(-\sum_i u_i\le0\). Hence all \(u_i=0\). A full-dimensional convex polytope has a nonzero supporting functional at every boundary point, so the origin cannot be on its boundary. This also verifies that the preceding list contains exactly all vertices. At any of those vertices, the unique exposing functional shows that a probability law having that mean must be its Dirac law.

For the root equation, the function \(q\mapsto q^{n+1}(1+q)^{n-1}\) is strictly increasing on \(q>0\), from zero to infinity. At \(q=\varphi^{-1}\), its value is \(\varphi^{-2}<1\), because \(\varphi^{-1}(1+\varphi^{-1})=1\). At \(q=5/6\), its value is at least its \(n=2\) value \(1375/1296>1\): writing it as \(q^2[q(1+q)]^{n-1}\) proves this comparison. The claimed unique root and uniform bounds follow. Its equation also gives
\(\log[q_n(1+q_n)]=-2\log q_n/(n-1)\longrightarrow0\).
The bounds keep \(\log q_n\) uniformly bounded, and \(q(1+q)\) is strictly increasing for \(q>0\); consequently \(q_n\to\varphi^{-1}\).

The proposed origin row is a probability law by its partition function. For any coordinate \(i\), the unnormalized sum of that coordinate over the Boolean part is \(q_n(1+q_n)^{n-1}\), and the unnormalized contribution from the apex is \(-q_n^{-n}\). The root equation says these cancel exactly. Therefore every coordinate mean is zero. To prove maximal entropy rather than merely feasibility, let \(\mu\) be any probability law on \(D_n\) with mean zero, and put \(K_n(\mathbf x)=\sum_i x_i\), the assignment's sum variable \(K\). On every support point, the proposed row has log probability \(K_n(\mathbf x)\log q_n-\log Z_n^\star\). Nonnegativity of relative entropy gives
\[
D(\mu\|\nu_{n,\mathbf0})
=-H(\mu)-\log q_n\,\mathbb E_\mu K_n+\log Z_n^\star
=\log Z_n^\star-H(\mu)\ge0,
\]
where \(H(\mu)=-\sum\mu\log\mu\). Equality holds only at the proposed row. Thus it is the unique maximum-entropy row and its entropy is exactly \(\log Z_n^\star\). Its common coordinate exponential tilt is \(\log q_n\). The other rows are the Dirac laws already verified geometrically. For the uniform original source, minimizing relative entropy is maximizing entropy, since \(D(\mu\|p_n)=\log N_n-H(\mu)\). Hence these are also precisely the rows required by the likelihood definition.

Apply the boundary-inclusive entropy-capacity identity of bf1ff94487296374, namely \(\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)=\exp[-D(\nu_{p,\mathbf j}\|p)]\). It gives \(Z_n^\star/N_n\) at the origin and \(1/N_n\) at every vertex. Summing \(p_{n,\mathbf j}\mathsf C_{p_n}(\mathbf j)^2\) gives the displayed exact \(\mathcal B_2(p_n)\), and its original capacity-weight formula gives the displayed \(\omega_{n,\mathbf0}\). There is one original root factor \(1/N_n\) in this sum, not a capacity-reweighted root factor.

The root equation permits the exact rewritings
\[
\begin{aligned}
q_n^{-n}&=q_n(1+q_n)^{n-1},
&Z_n^\star&=(1+q_n)^{n-1}(1+2q_n),\\
\nu_{n,\mathbf0}(-\mathbf1_n)&=\frac{q_n}{1+2q_n},
&\nu_{n,\mathbf0}(\{0,1\}^n)&=\frac{1+q_n}{1+2q_n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Conditional on the Boolean cube, the row is the product of Bernoulli laws of parameter \(q_n/(1+q_n)\). Thus \(K_n=-n\) at the apex and \(K_n\) is binomial on the conditional cube. Its mean is zero, and its second moment simplifies to
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{n,\mathbf0}}K_n
&=\frac{q_n}{1+2q_n}n^2
 +\frac{1+q_n}{1+2q_n}
    \left(\frac{nq_n}{(1+q_n)^2}
          +\frac{n^2q_n^2}{(1+q_n)^2}\right)\\
&=\frac{q_n}{1+q_n}n^2
  +\frac{q_n}{(1+q_n)(1+2q_n)}n.
\end{aligned}
\]
The log likelihood relative to the original uniform source is \(K_n\log q_n-\log Z_n^\star+\log N_n\), so its variance is \((\log q_n)^2\operatorname{Var}K_n\). At every Dirac row the log likelihood is constant on its positive support, hence its variance is zero. This proves the exact variance formulas. In particular \(V_{n,\mathbf0}\ge\frac13(\log(6/5))^2n^2\), using \(q_n>1/2\) and \(q_n<5/6\).

The partition-function rewrite and \(q_n\to\varphi^{-1}\) imply \((Z_n^\star)^{1/n}\to\varphi\). Therefore \(((Z_n^\star)^2/2^n)^{1/n}\to\varphi^2/2>1\), so this ratio tends to infinity and \(\omega_{n,\mathbf0}\to1\). The exact variance formula gives \(V_{n,\mathbf0}/n^2\to\varphi^{-2}(\log\varphi)^2\). Since only this row contributes to the weighted price, the claimed weighted limit follows. Finally, in the exact capacity-moment numerator, \((Z_n^\star)^2\) dominates \(N_n-1=2^n\), while \(N_n^{1/n}\to2\). Hence \((4^n\mathcal B_2(p_n))^{1/n}\to\varphi^2/2\). This establishes exponential capacity surplus, not merely strict surplus.

For completeness, the large likelihood variance is compatible with a uniform directional fourth-moment bound. Only the origin row needs checking. Write \(\xi_n=q_n/(1+q_n)\), \(\gamma_n=(1+q_n)/(1+2q_n)\), and \(v_n=\xi_n(1-\xi_n)\). These are, respectively, the conditional Bernoulli parameter, the cube probability, and the Bernoulli variance, not aliases of any predecessor's conversion constants. We have \(1/3<\xi_n<1/2\), \(\gamma_n>1/2\), \(v_n\ge2/9\), and \(1-\gamma_n+\gamma_n\xi_n^2=\xi_n\). For a fixed direction \(\mathbf u\), on the conditional cube let \(W=\sum_i u_i(B_i-\xi_n)\), where the \(B_i\) are independent Bernoulli variables. Since \(|B_i-\xi_n|\le1\), each fourth moment is at most \(u_i^4v_n\le(9/2)u_i^4v_n^2\). Expanding the fourth moment of an independent centered sum consequently gives \(\mathbb E W^4\le5(v_n\sum_i u_i^2)^2\).

The projection \(Y=\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf X\) is centered under the full origin row. Its variance is \(\gamma_n v_n\sum_i u_i^2+\xi_n(\sum_i u_i)^2\). At the apex it equals \(-\sum_i u_i\), and on the cube it equals \(W+\xi_n\sum_i u_i\). Applying \(|a+b|^4\le8(|a|^4+|b|^4)\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E Y^4
&\le\frac{40}{\gamma_n}
       \left(\gamma_n v_n\sum_i u_i^2\right)^2
 +\left(\frac{1-\gamma_n}{\xi_n^2}
                 +8\gamma_n\xi_n^2\right)
       \left(\xi_n\Bigl(\sum_i u_i\Bigr)^2\right)^2\\
&\le80\left(\gamma_n v_n\sum_i u_i^2
               +\xi_n\Bigl(\sum_i u_i\Bigr)^2\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, the first coefficient is at most \(80\), the second is at most \(9+8=17\), and both squared quantities are nonnegative. At every vertex row the centered projection is identically zero. This proves the stated all-row certificate, including zero-variance directions.

We next verify the actual moments directly. An exposing functional at a vertex produces a closed halfspace whose trace is that single vertex. Every containing halfspace has at least its root atom, so the depth at each vertex is exactly \(1/N_n\). Because the origin is interior, every proper closed halfspace containing it contains at least one additional support point. For example, after shifting the boundary parallel to itself through the origin, a nonzero normal has a strictly positive maximum on the full-dimensional polytope, attained at a support point different from the origin. Thus its depth is at least \(2/N_n\). The closed halfspace \(\{-\sum_i x_i\ge0\}\) has trace exactly \(\{\mathbf0,-\mathbf1_n\}\), proving equality. Averaging these depths with the original uniform law yields the exact displayed moments and origin fractions. Since \(N_n\le(3/2)2^n\), their lower bounds follow from \(\mathcal M_2(p_n)\ge N_n^{-2}\) and \(\mathcal M_3(p_n)\ge N_n^{-3}\). Their normalized limits follow from \(N_n/2^n\to1\).

It remains to establish the interval padding without assuming a product-entropy theorem. The convex hull of \(A_{n,L}\) is \(\mathcal P_n\times[0,L]\): products of convex-combination coefficients prove the nontrivial inclusion. Its integer points are exactly \(D_n\times I_L\), by the completeness just established and the interval's integer endpoints. The support differences include every coordinate unit vector, since \(L\ge1\), so its difference lattice is \(\mathbb Z^{n+1}\) and its rank is \(n+1\).

Fix an integer target \((\mathbf j,k)\in A_{n,L}\). Any law \(\mu\) on the product with that mean has marginal laws of means \(\mathbf j\) and \(k\). Entropy subadditivity here follows directly from nonnegative relative entropy to the product of these marginals:
\[
D(\mu\|\mu_D\otimes\mu_I)
=H(\mu_D)+H(\mu_I)-H(\mu)\ge0.
\]
Consequently its entropy is at most the sum of the two maximum marginal entropies. The product \(\nu_{n,\mathbf j}\otimes\nu_{\iota_L,k}\) has the required mean and attains that sum, so it is the entropy maximizer. Strict concavity of entropy, or uniqueness from bf1ff94487296374, makes it the unique row. The original product law is uniform and log-affine, so this is also its relative-entropy minimizing row. This proves the asserted product rows and exact integer means.

Use the capacity and capacity-moment factorization of c5abe3c72b8b89eb with its two block laws exactly \(p_n\) and \(\iota_L\). Substituting this factorization into the original capacity-weight definition yields
\(\omega_{P_{n,L},(\mathbf j,k)}=\omega_{n,\mathbf j}\omega_{\iota_L,k}\).
On the positive support of the product row, the log likelihood is the sum of the two factor log likelihoods. The row factors are independent, so
\[
\begin{aligned}
V_{P_{n,L},(\mathbf j,k)}
&=V_{n,\mathbf j}+V_{\iota_L,k},\\
\sum_{(\mathbf j,k)}\omega_{P_{n,L},(\mathbf j,k)}
                     V_{P_{n,L},(\mathbf j,k)}
&=\sum_{\mathbf j}\omega_{n,\mathbf j}V_{n,\mathbf j}
 +\sum_k\omega_{\iota_L,k}V_{\iota_L,k}
\ge\sum_{\mathbf j}\omega_{n,\mathbf j}V_{n,\mathbf j}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Both factor weight systems sum to one. Also \(I_L\) is complete of rank one with a log-affine law, so the baseline of bf1ff94487296374 gives \(\mathcal B_2(\iota_L)\ge1/4\). Capacity-moment factorization therefore gives the claimed surplus inequality for the padded law.

The actual depth supermultiplicativity proved in c5abe3c72b8b89eb applies to these original independent factors: \(\tau_{P_{n,L}}(\mathbf j,k)\ge\tau_{p_n}(\mathbf j)\tau_{\iota_L}(k)\). Raising to \(t=2,3\) and summing with the original product probabilities gives \(\mathcal M_t(P_{n,L})\ge\mathcal M_t(p_n)\mathcal M_t(\iota_L)\). Apply 8db3ba8c8761ea6c with one interval factor, its length \(m_1=L+1\ge2\), tilt \(\theta_1=0\), and intrinsic rank one. Its original law is precisely \(\iota_L\), and it gives \(\mathcal M_2(\iota_L)\ge a_{\mathrm{box}}^2/4\) and \(\mathcal M_3(\iota_L)\ge a_{\mathrm{box}}^3/8\), uniformly for all finite \(L\). Multiplying by the base moment bounds proves the padded moment bounds, with no capacity reweighting of the roots.

Finally, the displayed cardinality ratio follows exactly from \(|A_{n,L}|=N_n(L+1)\). The base weighted price divided by \(n^2\) converges to a positive constant, while the padded rank is only \(n+1\). The padded weighted price divided by rank therefore diverges for every choice of \(L_n\ge1\), in particular for all \(L_n\to\infty\). These exact families prove both stated bridge failures. Their actual moments stay at the required dimensional scales; thus neither failure is a counterexample to the locked target.
statement:
All logarithms are natural. For a finite complete support \(A\subseteq\mathbb Z^r\) of full affine dimension \(r\ge1\) and a strictly positive log-affine probability law \(p_{\mathbf x}=e^{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf x}/\sum_{\mathbf y\in A}e^{\boldsymbol\ell\cdot\mathbf y}\), with arbitrary \(\boldsymbol\ell\in\mathbb R^r\), retain the actual depth, entropy capacity, and original-law moments of accepted facts bf1ff94487296374 and c5abe3c72b8b89eb:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_p(\mathbf j)
&=\inf_{H\ni\mathbf j}\sum_{\mathbf x\in A\cap H}p_{\mathbf x},
&\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)
&=\inf_{\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^r}
  \sum_{\mathbf x\in A}p_{\mathbf x}
       e^{\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf x-\mathbf j)},\\
\mathcal B_2(p)
&=\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}p_{\mathbf j}\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)^2,
&\mathcal M_t(p)
&=\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}p_{\mathbf j}\tau_p(\mathbf j)^t
\quad(t=2,3).
\end{aligned}
\]
The depth infimum is over proper closed halfspaces. Let \(\nu_{p,\mathbf j}\) be the unique maximum-entropy law on \(A\) with mean \(\mathbf j\), and define
\[
\omega_{p,\mathbf j}
=\frac{p_{\mathbf j}\mathsf C_p(\mathbf j)^2}{\mathcal B_2(p)},
\qquad
V_{p,\mathbf j}
=\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{p,\mathbf j}}
  \left[\log\frac{\nu_{p,\mathbf j}(\mathbf X)}{p_{\mathbf X}}\right].
\]
The logarithm is evaluated only on the positive row support. Under \(p_i=p\), these are exactly \(\nu_{i,\mathbf j},\omega_{i,\mathbf j},V_{i,\mathbf j}\) of c5abe3c72b8b89eb. The row is also exactly \(r_{A,\mathbf j}\) of bf1ff94487296374 with its face-support argument \(E=A\), and exactly its relative-entropy minimizing row. These are aliases, not changes of root normalization. In particular, \(\omega_p\) is not the original law \(p\).

For every integer \(n\ge2\), let
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal P_n
&=\operatorname{conv}\bigl([0,1]^n\cup\{-\mathbf1_n\}\bigr),
&D_n&=\{0,1\}^n\cup\{-\mathbf1_n\},\\
N_n&=2^n+1,
&p_{n,\mathbf x}&=N_n^{-1}\quad(\mathbf x\in D_n).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\mathbf1_n=(1,\ldots,1)\), and \(\mathcal P_n\) is the polytope denoted \(P_n\) in the assignment; \(P\) below remains a product probability law. The support is complete, \(D_n=\mathcal P_n\cap\mathbb Z^n\), its difference lattice is \(\mathbb Z^n\), and its intrinsic rank is \(n\). Its vertices are precisely \(D_n\setminus\{\mathbf0\}\), and \(\mathbf0\) is interior to \(\mathcal P_n\). Write \(\nu_{n,\mathbf j},\omega_{n,\mathbf j},V_{n,\mathbf j}\) for the exact aliases \(\nu_{p_n,\mathbf j},\omega_{p_n,\mathbf j},V_{p_n,\mathbf j}\).

Let \(\varphi=(1+\sqrt5)/2\). There is a unique positive root \(q_n\) of \(q_n^{n+1}(1+q_n)^{n-1}=1\), and \(\varphi^{-1}<q_n<5/6\), with \(q_n\to\varphi^{-1}\). Set \(Z_n^\star=(1+q_n)^n+q_n^{-n}\), the exact alias of the assignment's \(Z^*\). The entropy row at the integer target \(\mathbf0\) is
\[
\nu_{n,\mathbf0}(\mathbf b)=\frac{q_n^{|\mathbf b|}}{Z_n^\star}
\quad(\mathbf b\in\{0,1\}^n),
\qquad
\nu_{n,\mathbf0}(-\mathbf1_n)=\frac{q_n^{-n}}{Z_n^\star},
\quad |\mathbf b|=\sum_i b_i.
\]
It has mean exactly \(\mathbf0\), not merely an asymptotically small mean. All other entropy rows are Dirac laws at their respective integer targets. The capacities, capacity weights, and likelihood variances satisfy
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf C_{p_n}(\mathbf0)&=\frac{Z_n^\star}{N_n},
&\mathsf C_{p_n}(\mathbf j)&=\frac1{N_n}
&& (\mathbf j\ne\mathbf0),\\
\mathcal B_2(p_n)&=\frac{N_n-1+(Z_n^\star)^2}{N_n^3},
&\omega_{n,\mathbf0}&=\frac{(Z_n^\star)^2}{N_n-1+(Z_n^\star)^2},\\
V_{n,\mathbf0}
&=(\log q_n)^2
  \left(\frac{q_n}{1+q_n}n^2
        +\frac{q_n}{(1+q_n)(1+2q_n)}n\right),
&V_{n,\mathbf j}&=0
&& (\mathbf j\ne\mathbf0).
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(Z_n^\star)^{1/n}&\longrightarrow\varphi,
&\omega_{n,\mathbf0}&\longrightarrow1,\\
\frac1{n^2}\sum_{\mathbf j\in D_n}\omega_{n,\mathbf j}V_{n,\mathbf j}
&\longrightarrow\varphi^{-2}(\log\varphi)^2>0,
&(4^n\mathcal B_2(p_n))^{1/n}
&\longrightarrow\frac{\varphi^2}{2}>1.
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover, every row satisfies the uniform directional fourth-moment bound
\[
\mathbb E_{\nu_{n,\mathbf j}}
 [(\mathbf u\cdot(\mathbf X-\mathbf j))^4]
\le80\left(\operatorname{Var}_{\nu_{n,\mathbf j}}
                    [\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf X]\right)^2
\quad(\mathbf j\in D_n,\ \mathbf u\in\mathbb R^n).
\]
The actual depths and moments of the original uniform source are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\tau_{p_n}(\mathbf0)&=\frac2{N_n},
&\tau_{p_n}(\mathbf j)&=\frac1{N_n}
&& (\mathbf j\ne\mathbf0),\\
\mathcal M_2(p_n)&=\frac{N_n+3}{N_n^3}
                  \ge(2/3)^2 4^{-n},
&\mathcal M_3(p_n)&=\frac{N_n+7}{N_n^4}
                  \ge(2/3)^3 8^{-n}.
\end{aligned}
\]
In fact \(4^n\mathcal M_2(p_n)\to1\) and \(8^n\mathcal M_3(p_n)\to1\). The origin's fractions of these actual moments are \(4/(N_n+3)\) and \(8/(N_n+7)\), respectively, both tending to zero, despite \(\omega_{n,\mathbf0}\to1\).

For any integer \(L\ge1\), let \(I_L=\{0,\ldots,L\}\), let \(\iota_L\) be its uniform law, and set \(A_{n,L}=D_n\times I_L\) and \(P_{n,L}=p_n\otimes\iota_L\). This is a complete support with difference lattice \(\mathbb Z^{n+1}\), intrinsic rank \(R=n+1\), and uniform original law. Its entropy rows are products of the corresponding factor rows, so every row mean is an integer point of \(A_{n,L}\). Its original capacity weights satisfy
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{(\mathbf j,k)\in A_{n,L}}
 \omega_{P_{n,L},(\mathbf j,k)}V_{P_{n,L},(\mathbf j,k)}
&\ge\sum_{\mathbf j\in D_n}\omega_{n,\mathbf j}V_{n,\mathbf j},\\
4^{n+1}\mathcal B_2(P_{n,L})
&\ge4^n\mathcal B_2(p_n),\\
\mathcal M_2(P_{n,L})
&\ge a_{\mathrm{box}}^2(2/3)^2 4^{-(n+1)},\\
\mathcal M_3(P_{n,L})
&\ge a_{\mathrm{box}}^3(2/3)^3 8^{-(n+1)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(a_{\mathrm{box}}>0\) is exactly the absolute constant of accepted fact 8db3ba8c8761ea6c, without any change in its normalization. Thus, for every sequence of integers \(L_n\ge1\) tending to infinity,
\[
\frac{|A_{n,L_n}|}{2^{n+1}}
=\frac{(1+2^{-n})(L_n+1)}2\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
\frac1{n+1}\sum_{(\mathbf j,k)\in A_{n,L_n}}
 \omega_{P_{n,L_n},(\mathbf j,k)}V_{P_{n,L_n},(\mathbf j,k)}
\longrightarrow\infty.
\]

In particular, the following universal bridge is false: there exists a finite absolute constant \(c_{\mathrm{price}}\) such that every finite complete full-dimensional \(A\subseteq\mathbb Z^r\) and every strictly positive log-affine original law \(p\) satisfy \(\sum_{\mathbf j\in A}\omega_{p,\mathbf j}V_{p,\mathbf j}\le c_{\mathrm{price}}r\). The base family disproves it even with directional fourth-moment constant \(80\) and any fixed prescribed capacity surplus \(\mathcal B_2(p)\ge g4^{-r}\), \(g>1\), for all sufficiently large \(n\). The padded family disproves a restriction based solely on making \(|A|/2^r\) arbitrarily large. No integral-mean condition is imposed on the original source law; the constrained means of all entropy rows are exactly integral.
